speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how is the public interest threshold of online statements of falsehoods determined and measured under the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA); (b) whether the Ministry will consider recommending that Ministers state which public interest criteria under section 7(1b) of POFMA are met and how so, when requesting for a direction to be issued; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider creating a central listing of all issued directions on the POFMA website.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the Ministry's position on perceptions of a partisan political bias over the recent applications of POFMA and how this may impact public trust in objectivity and independence of the Government's instruments of combatting online falsehoods; and (b) what steps are being taken to maintain public trust in light of such perceptions, especially given the critical role of public trust in buttressing society against coordinated, malicious fake news.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Government and, indeed, Members of this House have a duty to ensure that our citizens are not misled or misinformed by such falsehoods, and that is precisely why POFMA was enacted.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In all of the POFMA cases so far, Correction Directions have been issued.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These Directions require that the facts be placed alongside the original posts so that Singaporeans can read both versions and draw their own conclusions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Would the Member not agree that the best way to maintain public trust in the Government and our institutions is to juxtapose the truth with the falsehood, and allow our citizens to decide what the facts are?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And would the Member also not agree that the law should apply even if those who have put out the falsehoods thus far happen to have political affiliations?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Furthermore, POFMA requires that the Minister provide the basis in accordance with existing laws for her or his determination that a statement is a falsehood.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the recent cases, the falsehoods and the reasons for using POFMA were made clear in the clarifications that were issued by the respective Ministries.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If the recipient of the POFMA Direction disputes the facts, quick and inexpensive recourse to the Courts is available.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These provisions ensure transparency and accountability in the POFMA process.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All Government Corrections issued under POFMA are already compiled in a section of the Government’s fact-checking website, "Factually".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In addition, the POFMA Office website has a list of the press releases issued together with the POFMA Directions.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister had assured the House and the public in May last year when we were debating on the POFMA Bill that the Bill will not be far-reaching, using the example of the 39 takedown orders under the Broadcasting Act since 1996.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I think he mentioned that it was an average of one a year.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: POFMA has been used five times within a month, and just two months after coming into effect.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Will the Minister please clarify if this is considered far-reaching or not?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question I have is: the Minister has clarified that POFMA has a central listing on its website.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But could I ask the Minister to clarify if the POFMA Office will provide a full description of the public interest rationale each time that POFMA is used according to section 7(1b) of POFMA?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: There are actually six specific public interest thresholds that are listed there in the Act.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Last but not least, could I ask the Minister: we all agree that we are seeing an alarming rise of fake news.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister enlighten us on the number of fake news that are monitored and flagged by the POFMA Office and the various Ministries every month?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I know that Thailand's anti-fake news centre talked about 8,000 fake news that were monitored and flagged just within the month of November 2019 alone.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister assure the House and Singaporeans that the Ministries and the POFMA Office are also monitoring and flagging news to use POFMA on, whether non-partisan or partisan?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For example, the fake National University of Singapore (NUS) Facebook group ran for a while without being "POFMA-ed" until Facebook itself took it down.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, is the use of the legislation appropriate, measured and fit for purpose?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I do not think that you should go by the sheer number of times that it has been used in this period.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it is a confluence of factors that has led to that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But if you look at the facts of the matter, it is very simple.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Third, they have explained clearly – each Ministry in each of its Directions, it has issued a clear clarification as to what the falsehood is and why POFMA is being used, and that includes, therefore, a broad explanation as to what is the public interest consideration which is encompassed in there.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And thereafter, avenues of appeal are available, to the Minister, as indeed some have chosen to exercise, and the recourse to Courts is also available.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if you look at it in its totality, there is proportionality, there is fit for purpose and we have taken actions according to the situation as warranted.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member has asked about the public interest rationale according to section 7.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The fact of the matter is, and if you read the section carefully, it starts by saying "without detracting from the generality” of the point of “public interest" and then proceeds to list a few examples.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Those are intended to be illustrative, but they are not exhaustive.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What that means, therefore, is when the Act is exercised, the clarification and the explanation given in that clarification notice by the Minister will have the evidence to support the public interest case.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think the final point is on tracking and numbers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The first one is: does the identity of the person making the false statement matter for the public interest test, that is, independently of other factors?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And I would hope that the Minister could make clear that it is virality, the damage that the statement causes that matters and not who says it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Otherwise, I am very worried that it might look as if the Government is setting up speed traps where perhaps Opposition politicians drive but not elsewhere.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And that is a real concern, I think.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, would the Minister agree that for the falsehoods which are not viral or rapidly damaging – the slow drip problems – could it be more effective to combat these with education and information rather than a Correction Order?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And Parliament had agreed that these powers under POFMA were necessary to quickly correct falsehoods that might turn a spark into a flame.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But those powers do not seem as well-suited for educating the public about our financial Reserves or about our labour market policy.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think if you need an extension, the Leader of the House will move the extension.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Leader, would you like to move the extension?

The following questions were moved earlier 	— Ms Anthea Ong asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how is the public interest threshold of online statements of falsehoods determined and measured under the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA); (b) whether the Ministry will consider recommending that Ministers state which public interest criteria under section 7(1b) of POFMA are met and how so, when requesting for a direction to be issued; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider creating a central listing of all issued directions on the POFMA website.

Ms Anthea Ong asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the Ministry's position on perceptions of a partisan political bias over the recent applications of POFMA and how this may impact public trust in objectivity and independence of the Government's instruments of combatting online falsehoods; and (b) what steps are being taken to maintain public trust in light of such perceptions, especially given the critical role of public trust in buttressing society against coordinated, malicious fake news.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I think the Member had a few questions on, first, the question was the identity of the person or entity who puts out the falsehood matter.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As I have explained very clearly the process, and I think this was widely convassed during the debate on the Second Reading, the focus is on the fact, or falsehood as it were, in accordance, and do we have the existing legislation that backs that assessment; and secondly, whether there is a public interest concerned that merits action.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: That is a judgement made by the Minister, the domain Minister advised by his officials.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Therefore, the answer is – and I think what the Member is alluding to is the fact that the first few POFMA actions appear to have been issued against individuals who are either politicians or affiliated with political party or political parties.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I would say that that is a convergence, some might say unfortunate convergence or coincidence, but also indicates to a certain pattern of communication that exists out there.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But whatever the case may be, that is the situation today.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But it does not mean that that is going to be the situation going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Because, ultimately, whether there is a falsehood, there is a public threshold and, if so, then what is the appropriate course of action.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The point was also made about falsehoods that are not viral, whether we can use alternative mechanisms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I think in talking about, in discussing this matter, we have to look by virality, which was one of the points, but remember we also talked about the virulence of the falsehood.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And you have to take both into account, because there will be instances where the nature of the falsehood is such that it goes to the core of the credibility and the standing of our institutions and it deserves a response under POFMA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And such a response has the additional impact of ensuring that future such commentary would be guided or advised by this action.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, there is a multiplicity of factors, and I think it would be a too blunt to just look at it in terms of one criterion, like virality.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Having said that, I think the Member's point was: do we have alternative mechanisms?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And I want to assure him that we continue to be actively involved in the education of our citizens on this matter.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In fact, both Ms Anthea Ong and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira have raised this point before during the Second Reading.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is an important point that we have an educated, discerning citizenry and we must ensure they are well-informed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I would add that we have also, if Members would have noticed, in some cases issued statements rather than a POFMA direction.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And that has also occurred in the last several weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, I think if you look at it in totality, we have to take into account the overall impact and then we have to consider what is the proportionate response and then be prepared to take it and, if it so happens that some of the people involved are politically affiliated, well, that is the consequence of their actions.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In terms of the thousands of fake news that are possibly floating around the Internet – and the Minister has turned my question around to answer my other question which is pretty brilliant, I must say – yes, it does not seem far-reaching when you turned it around to say that way.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But my question was actually, given that there are thousands of fake news floating around in the Web, does the POFMA Office monitor and flag the non-partisan news and statements that are made?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Because there are so many out there, one of which that came to my mind was the fake NUS group and we did not do anything until Facebook took it down themselves.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, my concern is – and the Minister could be right it could just be a convergence of consequences and circumstances – to have four or five POFMA 	directions that are so partisan in nature, you would understand why there are really genuine concerns from the ground, especially like I said, there are actually thousands of fake news out there that could also be in the public interest to actually POFMA them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I was merely using the facts that the Member cited to make the case.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But in some way, it is no different for the other kinds of activities that we have, too.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The other point was, what was it again?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I was not sure what the Member was getting to.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: There are thousands of fake news out there that are non-partisan but actually are in the public interest to be POFMA-ed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is an interesting point because the Member seems to be making the argument that, if instead of four against the previous four cases, we now had eight and four were non-partisan, that would look better?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I would say that, basically, we monitor.
